question: Spirit A uses Powerstorm on Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares. Afterwards Bringer uses Call on Midnight’s Dream in a legal land with Dahan, gains a Fast Major Power, Forgets Call on Midnight’s Dream for the Major gain, and uses its conditional permission to play the new Major immediately. Bringer then uses that new Major normally. Assume sufficient Energy, valid targets, and no other restrictions. May Bringer spend the previously granted Powerstorm Repeat on this new Major even though it was not in play when Powerstorm resolved?
answer: Yes. Powerstorm grants the Spirit a general once-this-turn Repeat option, not a permission restricted to cards already in play at grant time. The new Major is eligible once it is in play; Bringer can pay its cost and Repeat it at its current Speed. Forgetting Call on Midnight’s Dream does not remove the separate new Major.
source_refs: Primary original Powerstorm and Call on Midnight’s Dream faces in card-scope-source/
new_coverage: The FAQ expressly defines the grant-to-use temporal eligibility boundary. This is an independently published permission, beyond combining extra-play arithmetic with deferred selection. The scenario demonstrates that permission without inventing a new rule.
why_not_previously_requested: Q40 asks whether the Repeat card must be chosen immediately, whether it can be Slow/an Innate, and whether printed Elements recur. A respondent may correctly allow later choice among the grant-time cards while wrongly excluding cards played afterwards. Q37/Q38 ask gaining and extra-play timing, with no Repeat eligibility question. Q88 asks the opposite departure branch: the Forgotten original card cannot later be Repeated. Q41/Q42/Q43/Q95/Q106/Q107/Q111/Q114 concern modifiers, chaining, destination, Speed, counts, use limits, or retargeting; none asks whether a later entrant can receive an earlier Repeat permission.
core_applicability: Original Powerstorm and Call on Midnight’s Dream printed faces have no expansion mark. Call on Midnight’s Dream explicitly supplies the later Major gain/play; no expansion producer is imported. The named Major may be any original-core Fast Major meeting the stated assumptions.

question: In a standard core game a land is already crowded with Invaders, Dahan, and Spirit Presence. Can a general per-land stacking limit prevent an otherwise legal Build, Gather, or Presence placement there? Do any of those three types of piece have such a default cap?
answer: No. There is no default stacking limit for any piece, so crowding alone cannot prevent those otherwise legal additions or movements. Each specific action must still obey its normal instructions. A large Presence stack still forms only one Sacred Site for that Spirit in that land.
source_refs: CORE p.13 Presence; default no per-land limits
new_coverage: This is an explicit spatial-capacity permission for all piece types, distinct from inventory availability and Sacred Site counting. The candidate uses no numerical variants and tests one general rule.
why_not_previously_requested: Q23 asks mixed-Spirit Sacred Site ownership, whether four Presence create two sites, and the meaning of your land. It establishes the site-counting outcome for that particular stack, without asking a default land-cap rule. Q22 asks whether setup placements may share a land. Q33 asks whether Dahan/Invaders are limited by the physical supply, which is a global component-availability rule and leaves a distinct per-land-cap misconception untested. The other movement/build questions never request whether existing crowding prohibits an otherwise legal action.
core_applicability: The ruling explicitly describes the default game and names Adversary/Scenario caps as exceptions. Those excluded exceptions are not invoked. CORE p.13 independently permits any number of Presence in a land.
